## Verdict and scope

**Verdict: equivalent.** The author handoff and assembled mathematical bodies faithfully explain the four frozen roots. The primary conclusion is the corrected explicit-family comparison: for every real \(\lambda>1\), the constant \(\gamma_\lambda\) is positive, and for every \(0<h\leq1\) there is a real \(r\) satisfying
\[
0<r<h,\qquad A_\lambda(E_r)=A_\lambda(C_h),\qquad P_\lambda(C_h)-P_\lambda(E_r)>\frac{\gamma_\lambda}{h}>0.
\]
The separately named scalar comparison, the complete elementary route, and unconditional geometric realization are also present with their frozen hypotheses and quantifier order. Neither equal area nor an area/perimeter bridge is assumed by the primary theorem. [@lean:CMVElementary.geometric_comparison] [@lean:CMVElementary.scalar_comparison] [@lean:CMVElementary.elementary_route] [@lean:CMVElementary.geometric_realization]

The review covers every one of the 506 inventoried non-generated declarations, both author prose fields, all declaration statements and explanations, and both assembled Markdown manuscripts. The supplied original note is a source to be corrected, not the literal theorem being certified. The unrestricted classification corollary remains explicitly informal and dependent on cited external results.

## Evidence and elementary proof route

The checked statements preserve the strict density hypothesis, the closed right endpoint of the four-arc curvature interval, and the strictly smaller positive competitor parameter. The margin is the specified density-dependent constant divided by curvature; no positive lower bound uniform as \(\lambda\downarrow1\) is asserted. The scalar functions remain total real definitions, while geometric and differential claims use their stated domains. The symbol \(j\) denotes the explicitly defined continuous extension, not an endpoint differentiation operation. [@lean:CMVElementary.ScalarStatement] [@lean:CMVElementary.GeometricStatement] [@lean:CMVElementary.jprime]

The radical normalization is proved for positive density. Interior differentiation gives
\[
S'(z)=-2D(z),\qquad J'(u)=j(u),\qquad H(u)=J(u)-uj(u).
\]
Evenness and strict increase of \(D\) determine the signs of \(j\). Equal endpoint values give the lower bound for \(J\). On the closed lower third, the actual proof of the lower bound for \(H\) uses the decreasing-derivative tangent lemma with independently proved premises. It does not project the desired bound from the record it is constructing. On the remaining interval it uses \(H\geq J\). The manuscript correctly distinguishes that dependency from the separately established derivative and limit identities for \(H\). [@lean:CMVElementary.DerivativePilot.sqrt_normalization] [@lean:CMVElementary.hasDerivAt_S] [@lean:CMVElementary.hasDerivAt_J] [@lean:CMVElementary.MonotoneTangent.h_lower_third_of_monotone_tangent] [@lean:CMVElementary.H_lower] [@lean:CMVElementary.auxiliary_claims]

The algebraic same-curvature identities yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
A_4(h)-A_3(h)&\geq\gamma_\lambda/h^2>0,\\
[P_4(h)-hA_4(h)]-[P_3(h)-hA_3(h)]&\geq\gamma_\lambda/h>0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The variational identity is transported by neighborhood equality with the normalized scalar library, rather than by equality at a single point. Divergence of the three-arc area chooses a positive left endpoint. The continuous equal-area level set in a compact interval has a greatest element. Its maximality and the intermediate value theorem give the strict area barrier to its right. No root uniqueness or global area monotonicity is used. [@lean:CMVElementary.same_curvature_claims] [@lean:CMVElementary.three_arc_eventuallyEq] [@lean:CMVElementary.three_arc_variational_hasDerivAt] [@lean:CMVElementary.A3_tendsto_atRight_zero] [@lean:CMVElementary.exists_greatest_level_root]

For the same selected root and fixed target area, the support expression satisfies
\[
Q(t)=P_3(t)+t[A_4(h)-A_3(t)],\qquad Q'(t)=A_4(h)-A_3(t)>0\quad(r<t<h).
\]
Continuity on the closed comparison interval gives \(Q(r)<Q(h)\). Combining this strict improvement with the non-strict same-curvature lower bound gives the strictly greater perimeter margin in the scalar root. Differentiation remains inside the interval even when \(h=1\). [@lean:CMVElementary.greatest_root_claims] [@lean:CMVElementary.strict_support_comparison] [@lean:CMVElementary.scalar_comparison]

## Model and geometry fidelity

The area is the Lebesgue integral of the piecewise constant density. The complete-frontier perimeter is determined by Euclidean one-dimensional Hausdorff measure. The coordinate product type is transported to its Euclidean realization before that Hausdorff measure is formed; the default maximum product metric is not used for arc length. The interfaces \(y=\pm1\) have density one. The generic perimeter functional accepts a measure, but the final geometric roots instantiate it with the canonical measure of the specified carrier. [@lean:StripDensity] [@lean:WeightedArea] [@lean:EuclideanPlane] [@lean:FrontierMeasure] [@lean:WeightedPerimeter]

The four-arc and three-arc sets are defined by literal disk, half-plane and horizontal-section inequalities. Exact carrier equalities connect these definitions to the integral infrastructure. The four-arc lower cap is the horizontal-axis reflection of the upper cap and lies in \(y\leq-1\); its non-endpoint exterior arc lies strictly below that interface. Strict attaching-chord points are interior to the assembled regions, whereas the entire three-arc bottom segment remains exposed frontier. [@lean:CMVElementary.GeometryBridge.C_assembly] [@lean:CMVElementary.GeometryBridge.E_assembly] [@lean:CMVElementary.GeometryBridge.reflected_cap_below] [@lean:OneSidedCircularCap.arcPoint_in_open_side] [@lean:CMVElementary.GeometryBridge.four_upper_chord] [@lean:CMVElementary.GeometryBridge.four_lower_chord] [@lean:CMVElementary.GeometryBridge.three_strict_chord] [@lean:CMVElementary.GeometryBridge.E_bottom_frontier]

The full cap-angle range retains major exterior caps for \(r<1/2\). At \(r=1/2\), the carrier is exactly the radius-two disk centered at \((0,1)\), and the bottom segment is a singleton of zero length, not a deleted or pinched branch. The four-arc endpoint \(h=1\) is included; its selected competitor still satisfies \(r<1\). Closedness, boundedness, measurability, density integrability and finite frontier mass are conclusions of the realization proofs. The geometric area formulas are actual carrier integral identities. The canonical perimeter formulas use exact frontier decompositions, actual Euclidean arc and segment lengths, and null pairwise junction overlaps. Auxiliary modeled or parametrized perimeter sums are explicitly bridged to those integrals before use. The bottom interface contributes its full density-one segment length. The realization records are constructed from the density and curvature bounds and are not supplied as hypotheses to evade those bridges. ## External-source checks

Cañete, Miranda Jr. and Vittone, *Some isoperimetric problems in planes with density*, Journal of Geometric Analysis **20** (2010), 243–290, is identified by the supplied `Canete2010.pdf` and the article's arXiv identifier. The inspected copy is the preprint `arXiv:0906.1256v1`; its SHA-256 is `0ee9b4787aa3c09f9a4ed05fb66563a820cd13596af401b76e7900e597711230`. The cited locators are substantive and exact: Section 2 for reduced-boundary perimeter; Lemma 3.8 and its proof, Step 2, for the candidate families and horizontal symmetry of the four-arc case; Proposition 3.9 for vertical reflection symmetry of arbitrary minimizers; Conjecture 3.12 for the proposed classification; and Theorem 3.16 for the remaining area ranges and transition coexistence. The latter leaves the four-arc alternative, which the corrected explicit-family theorem excludes after the cited identification.

The supplied note by Skilyn Leon, Rosa Pavlak, Evelyn Pulla and Xi Sisi Shen is identified by `CMV_Strip_Density_Problem.pdf`, its two Theorem 1 statements, Sections 3–6 and Remarks 1–3. Its checked SHA-256 is `d04a2e8e2ad45fe505345037c046ceaeb2a8d63b9e2b1c1eeb020b5251c576ff`, exactly the frozen original. The original Theorem 1 on page 2 and equation (3.2) on page 3 print the erroneous area-minus-perimeter expression. The handoff explicitly corrects both to perimeter minus perimeter and leaves the source PDF unchanged. Page 3 was also rendered and inspected to resolve the text-extraction warning; it explicitly states the agreement of complete and reduced boundaries up to a length-null set for its piecewise smooth Jordan regions. The new manuscript correctly acknowledges that this boundary statement was already in the draft.

The informal corollary does not conflate complete-frontier perimeter with the perimeter of arbitrary area-equivalent representatives. For these explicit piecewise-circular regions, agreement with reduced-boundary perimeter is a conventional geometric transfer; for arbitrary minimizers, the cited classification and regular-representative results must first be invoked. This transfer and the external classification are not extra Lean hypotheses or axioms. No uniqueness of minimizers is inferred, and transition coexistence is retained.

## Disposition

Accept the author handoff and the assembled mathematical bodies as equivalent to the frozen package claim. No mathematical, citation or author-body format revision is required by this pass. Acceptance is limited to the corrected explicit-family theorem and its three named supporting roots; the cited classification corollary remains informal, and the unchanged source note's two false printed displays remain explicitly uncertified.
